hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: The atlas → What is still missing Thirteen questions , several answered and one closed — and the oldest still open. Who Gerthardus Lodewikus Booysen's parents were; whether the County Cork the family speaks of is real at all. Three enquiries are out and unanswered: the Western Cape Archives, the National Archives in Pretoria, and the SANDF Documentation Centre, which has delivered half of what was asked. The list, and what would close each one, is at Open questions . Nothing here is taken on trust because it appears in a family tree.

hits.title: The line
hits.text: Seven generations up, the male line simply ends. One thing has changed here, and it is worth being precise about how little. Until the 1876 Sterfkennis was read, generation seven existed only because a family tree said so. It now exists because a nineteenth-century clerk wrote "Gerthardus Lödewikus Booijsen" and "Magdalena de Beer" on his son's death notice. See the line → That converts an assertion into a record. It does not add a generation. The buttons above him are still empty, the dates below are still arithmetic, and the question of who his own parents were is exactly as open as it was. What can be said is arithmetic rather than evidence.

hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: All three are checkable. Forty-four Cape colonists were executed for high treason , and that list is closed. What would settle it → What is not in dispute It is worth ending on this. The direct descent itself is unbroken and well sourced from Gerthardus Lodewikus Booysen to David Defranceski. The contradictions above sit on side branches, spouses' records and dates of death — not on the parent-to-child links of the line. Nothing on this page moves anybody out of the family. The single exception is the Barry line above 1819 , where the link to a father genuinely fails.

petrus-jacobus-booysen.r: Married at about seventeen; died a widower in the Transvaal, eighty-eight years old, on a farm called Brakfontein. His Sterfkennis — No. 678, written 14 September 1876 — is the oldest document about this family that this archive has read, it names his parents, and it lists eight children. Estate: NOTHING. “Niets nagelaten. Niets bekend.”

also.r: Farmer at Zevenfontein, Brak River. Signed his wife's 1863 death notice. Died fifteen years before the war.

david-schalk-booijsen.r: First on his father's 1876 death notice, and a major — and now with a date. His baptism of 4 JANUARY 1807 names his parents as PIETER JACOBUS BOOIJZEN and ANNA MARIA VAN DER MERWE, which is the only document in this archive that puts Anna Maria in the family at all. His father was eighteen when he was born. He married ADRIANA CHRISTINA VILJOEN — on 3 NOVEMBER 1828 AT CRADOCK, a date and a place this archive did not have until WikiTree was read on 13 September 2026, and FROM WIKITREE, NOT FROM A DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS READ — and named a daughter ANNA MARIA in 1835, after his own mother. His nephew, born 1848, carries the same name — the two are told apart only by a generation.

jan-gerthardus-lodewikus-booijsen.r: Fifth on his father’s 1876 notice, and named for the man at the top of the line. HIS is the estate TAB MHG O/2899, which this archive had spent months attributing to his nephew of the same name born in 1855 — the Transvaal probate index gives him as the deceased, aged 67, born district Graaff-Reinet, died 25 May 1885 at Vaalbank in the district of Lichtenburg. His daughter Magdalena Susanna Maria died on the same farm in 1920, and her death notice names him. He is how this family reaches the western Transvaal.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: The date had no source except the file number. The Transvaal probate index names the estate's deceased in full: Jan Gerardus Lodewicus Booijzen, aged 67, born district Graaff-Reinet, died 25 May 1885 at Vaalbank, district Lichtenburg — born about 1818, which is his UNCLE, fifth on the 1876 Sterfkennis. The nephew's death date is withdrawn and nothing is known about what became of him. The particular error is worth naming: the archive read a year off a reference number, wrote it in as a fact, and then cited the fact back.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Child, as written What this archive already knew David Schalk Booijsen — Magdalena Johanna Booijsen — Petrus Jacobus Booijsen generation five , b. 10 May 1812, the farmer at Zevenfontein who signed the 1863 death notice Anna Eliezabet Booijsen — Jan Gerthardus Lodewikus Booijsen — Eliezabet Cornelia Booijsen — Hendrik Stefanus Booijsen signed this notice Anna Maria Booijsen — Seven of these eight were unknown to this archive an hour ago. And three of the names — David Schalk , Magdalena Johanna , Jan Gerthardus Lodewikus — are the same names that appear on the 1863 death notice as children of Petrus Jacobus the younger , born 1848, 1853 and 1855.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: That sentence had no source except the estate reference itself. The archive read the year off the file number, wrote it into his life as a death date, and then quoted the death date back as if it were evidence. FamilySearch's index of the same Transvaal probate series gives the estate's deceased in full: What the index says Name Jan Gerardus Lodewicus Booijzen Relationship Deceased Age 67 Birthplace Distrik Graaf Reinet — birth year about 1818 Died 25 May 1885 Death place Vaalbank, distrik Lichtenburg ark 1:1:QPTJ-R6KB and 1:1:Q2DG-52P9 , two index passes over the same estate. magdalena-susanna-maria-van-den-berg.n: Magdalena Susanna Maria van den Berg
magdalena-susanna-maria-van-den-berg.r: His daughter, and the first person in the western Transvaal this archive can attach to the line rather than merely set beside it. Her 1920 Sterfkennis — estate 44420, stamped Pretoria 16 August 1920 — names her parents as Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus Booyzen and Magdalena Susanna Maria, gives her age as 59 years 9 months, and lists seven children. Her son-in-law B. J. van den Berg signed it.

pages.t: Magdalena Susanna Maria van den Berg

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: Lichtenburg joins the line · Found The same correction does the opposite favour. Vaalbank, in the district of Lichtenburg, is where the 1876 man's son died in 1885 — and this archive had already read a 1920 Sterfkennis from that farm for Magdalena Susanna Maria van den Berg, born Booyzen about 1860, father entered as Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus Booyzen, filed under “NOT PROVED”. She is his daughter. Two deaths on one farm thirty-five years apart, which is settlement rather than passage. Read west along the atlas: Rustenburg 1876, Lichtenburg 1885 and 1920, Marico 1903.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: The direct ancestor died in district Rustenburg in 1876 — twenty-five years before the war, a generation before Johannesburg. Two other notices read the same afternoon sit in the same country: a Magdalena Susanna Maria van den Berg, born Booyzen , who died at Vaalbank in the district of Lichtenburg in 1920 and whose father is entered as Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus Booyzen ; and an an Anna Johanna Booijzen , born in the district of Cradock about 1823, who died on a farm in the district of Rustenburg in 1891, leaving children called Petrus Jacobus, Magdalena Johanna and Hendrik Stephanus Nicolaas.

hendrik-stefanus-booijsen.r: Seventh on the 1876 notice — and the man who signed it, four lines under his own name, beside the veldkornet. His own death notice, TAB estate 14380, names HIS mother as ELIZABETHA BOOYSEN, BORN VAN DER MERWE — which resolves this archive’s oldest “Serious” contradiction, because his father’s recorded wife Anna Maria van der Merwe died three years before he was born. A FARMER, “Dutch”, married twice — Anna Catharina Johanna Olivier, then Charlotta Elizabetha Dormehl — and married last at ZEERUST, in the district of Marico. He died in his son-in-law’s house.

Hendrik Stephanus Booysen's own 1908 death notice — Transvaal estate 14380 — names his mother as ELIZABETHA BOOYSEN, BORN VAN DER MERWE, and gives his age as seventy-nine years eleven months at 11 May 1908, which puts his birth about June 1828, three years after the first wife died. hits.title: The namesakes
hits.text: Who When What they are to the name Robert Byron Keys b. 3 Jan 1878 Eldest of the eight Keys children by Johanna Catharina Mountjoy. Lancelott Byron Keys b. 29 Jan 1888 The second Byron. The name comes from the Keys side, not the Mountjoy. Coenrad Sybert van Staden — A son of Charlotta Dormehl by her FIRST husband. Johannes Sybert Roos — A son of the same woman by her SECOND husband. SYBERT crossing between two marriages of one woman. What it costs The same habit that makes this family legible makes it dangerous to index. Three of this archive's corrections are name collisions , and one of them stood for weeks: an estate filed in 1885 was given to the wrong Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus, and a death date was invented to fit.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Not one Booysen among them. Two van Stadens — Jacob Alewyn and Coenrad Sybert . Four Rooses — Gert Johannes , Matthys Johannes , Johannes Sybert , and Anna Francisa , married in community of property to Gert Johannes Laubeschagne. All of age. And after ten years of marriage to Hendrik Stefanus Booysen, no child of his is named , because she was fifty-one when she married him. This archive spent a month drawing his four children under her. Earlier today the 1892 marriage register — her age, her condition — made that impossible. Her own death notice now says the same thing from the other side, in her husband’s handwriting.

She is named again, and readably, on the 1935 Sterfkennis of their son Diederik Arnoldus, where both she and Ockert are entered OORLEDE. Two sons documented: Hendrik Stephanus Nicolaas, baptised 1882, and Diederik Arnoldus, born about August 1887.

diederik-arnoldus-booysen.r: A KARWEIER — a transport rider — of Zwartruggens, and a son of Ockert Johannes Stephanus Booysen and Elizabeth Johanna Sophia Myburgh. His Sterfkennis 87882 is the first document in this archive printed in Afrikaans rather than Dutch or English, and the first Booysen estate here worth more than £300. He married Elizabeth Anna Bronkhorst, widow Joubert, in community of property; their youngest son carries his grandfather’s name.

hendrik-stephanus-nicolaas-booyen.r: Baptised at Rustenburg on 30 January 1882, son of Ockert Johannes Stephanus Booysen and Elisabetta Johanna Sophia Myburgh — and named for his uncle, who was then twenty and would be dead at Brakfontein before the boy turned ten. He outlived that uncle by sixty-eight years.

anna-catharina-johanna-olivier.v: Anna Johanna Booijzen, gebooren Oliefier (1891) · Anna Catrena (1891) · born Olivier (1908)
anna-catharina-johanna-olivier.r: THE FIRST WIFE OF HENDRIK STEFANUS BOOIJSEN, and for a week this archive had her filed as a stranger. Her own Sterfkennis 6332 gives her parents as OCKEN JOHANNES OLIEFIER and ANNA JOHANNA BOTHA, her age as 67 years 8 months and 1 day, her farm as BRAKFONTEIN — which this archive read as Boekfontein — and her surname as OLIEFIER, which this archive read as Alberts. She was still married when she died: her husband outlived her by seventeen years and remarried at Zeerust eleven months later. Seven children, all of age: Petrus Jacobus, Ocken Johannes, Anna Johanna Maria, Elesabettha Maria Cornelya, Alettha Catrina Johanna, Magdalena Johanna, Hendrick Stefanus Nicolaas. Her father is where OCKERT JOHANNES came into this family — and her 1824 baptism gives his name entire, OCKERT JOHANNES STEPHANUS OLIVIER, which is exactly what her son was called. She married Hendrik Stephanus Booijzen at POTCHEFSTROOM on 3 JULY 1850, entry 206, she 25 and he 23 — the earliest evidence this archive has of this family north of the Vaal, twenty-six years before the 1876 death at Rustenburg and two years before the Sand River Convention.

What was withdrawn → Since then the second of those two has been settled. The farm is Brakfontein , not Boekfontein, and the maiden name is Oliefier , not Alberts. She is Anna Catharina Johanna Olivier , the first wife of Hendrik Stefanus Booijsen, and she died on the family's own farm. How that was read → 1937–38 · A whole estate, from the death to the last shilling Estates 58379 and 58380 , KAB MOOC 6/9/5047 — on this archive's Sources page as "Located, not yet read" for months. anna-maria-van-der-merwe.r: WikiTree makes her a daughter of DAVID SCHALK VAN DER MERWE and ANNA ELIZABETH LOUW—which, if right, is where the forename DAVID SCHALK entered this family: her eldest son carries her father’s names entire.FROM WIKITREE, NOT FROM A DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS READ, and it is checkable against the van der Merwe baptism registers rather than the tree. His wife, married 1805 at Graaff-Reinet — and DOCUMENTED, which she was not until today. A Dutch Reformed baptism of 4 JANUARY 1807 names her as the mother of DAVID SCHALK BOOIJZEN, born 12 December 1806, who is FIRST of the eight children on the 1876 Sterfkennis. That resolves a contradiction this archive marked Serious (they were married by 1806, so the 1825 Cape Town marriage record is a different couple) and it rewrites the wall on the ancestor chart, which said only a family tree put her there. WHAT IS STILL NOT PROVED is that she is the mother of the 1812 man in the direct line.

hits.text: The Brixton register keeps Years, Months and Days in three separate columns and FamilySearch's index collapses them into one field, so a child with the Years column blank comes out as “0 days”. This archive printed the index reading for an afternoon without opening the page. → reading Only a family tree puts Anna Maria van der Merwe in this family A Dutch Reformed baptism does. Her son DAVID SCHALK BOOIJZEN was born 12 December 1806 and christened on 4 January 1807, with PIETER JACOBUS BOOIJZEN and ANNA MARIA VAN DER MERWE named as his parents — and he is first of the eight on the 1876 Sterfkennis. hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: But “Serious”, not resolved — two men of one name in one town is precisely the mistake this archive keeps catching itself in, and the 1940 notice still names nobody. The inferred row stands, flagged, until a document settles it. → Anna Maria van der Merwe — married 1805 or 1825? The tree marries her to Petrus Jacobus Booysen in 1805 at Graaff-Reinet and has her dead “before March 1825”. FamilySearch carries a Dutch Reformed marriage of PETRUS JACOBUS BOOŸZEN and ANNA MARIA VAN DER MERWE dated 9 MARCH 1825, at Cape Town, indexed three separate times. Resolved RESOLVED, 13 September 2026.

hits.title: Open questions
hits.text: Page 78 then gives her husband as JAN BOOIJSEN, baptised 29 January 1741, and their SEVENTH CHILD as “Petrus Jacobus, gedoopt 21 September 1788, gehuwd met Anna Maria van der Merwe”, whose first child is “David Schalk, gedoopt 4 Januari 1807”. FOUR FIELDS AGREE WITH THIS ARCHIVE AND THE FIFTH IS THE FATHER. There is exactly one Petrus Jacobus of 21 September 1788 in the whole volume and exactly one David Schalk of 4 January 1807, and the word Lodewikus appears nowhere in it.

Lady Grey, which this archive already knows “Lady Grey, near Aliwal North, Cape Colony.” That is the family’s own church. Willem Hermanus “William Henry” Booyzen married Catherine Maria Sophia “Kathleen” Barry at Lady Grey on 22 December 1879. And David Schalk Booysen, born 9 June 1848, is his brother — fourth on the 1863 death notice of their mother Johanna Catharina Mountjoy, where Willem Hermanus is sixth. Two brothers married out of one small Cape church; one went east to the coal at Indwe and died there in 1905, the other went north to Pretoria.

hits.text: Fatal George Kolbe died in 1844 and Margaret Downing in 1867. Neither can be in a photograph taken in the late 1870s. hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: The women are not. Mountjoy (1838). Barry (1879). Kinnear (1940s). Behind the Barrys, Kolbe — a German tailor's family out of Soho who sailed as 1820 Settlers and named a Karoo farm Wurtemburg . Behind the Kolbes, Downing . That is why David Defranceski's great-grandfather, born on a farm in the Eastern Cape in 1901, was christened George Downing Mountjoy Booyzen . Every one of those forenames is a woman's surname. The women → And it is why the tree folds back on itself: in 1924 George married his own first cousin once removed , so his daughter Catherine descends from one Barry–Kolbe couple twice over. The cousin marriage → Corrections are the most valuable thing anyone can send.

hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: Resolved RESOLVED. His 1845 death notice (estate 7698) and his gravestone both give 1 December 1844, and neither his notice nor his widow’s 1867 notice lists a Julia. Reject the child, keep the date. The same two documents also drop KEETOR PETER BENJAMIN KOLBE, whom the tree gives a 1840 birth — he is in neither list. → George Downing Mountjoy Booyzen (1901–1947) Death dated 21 February 1947, with burial ten months later on 14 December 1947. Resolved RESOLVED by his death notice: he died 11 December 1947 and was buried on the 14th. “21 February” is the date the notice was signed — in 1948. A transcriber merged the two and lost ten months.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: They are the same woman, and the archive's earlier claim of "two Barry sisters marrying Booysens" is withdrawn . 1947 · George's death notice corrects his own death date Signed by G. Booyzen at Johannesburg on 21 February 1948 under the Administration of Estates Act 1913. Death Notice of George Downing Mountjoy Booyzen , died 11 December 1947 at Forest Hill, Johannesburg. "The day of the decease: On 11th December 1947 " — died at 85 Rheeden St, Forest Hill , Johannesburg. He died on 11 December 1947 — not 21 February 1947. 21 February is the date the notice was signed , and it was signed in 1948 . A transcriber conflated the two and lost ten months.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: There is no photograph of their farm, and this archive does not invent one. This archive was built for David Defranceski , born in Johannesburg, living in Brisbane. It runs backwards from his grandmother Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen (1929–2013) — who married Nuno Fernando Lerena at St Joseph's, Mayfair, in 1949 — into the north-eastern Cape: to Barkly East and Dordrecht , to Cradock and Graaff-Reinet , and out again to Württemberg , to Soho , and to a County Cork that may or may not be real. It is a public archive with one rule: the living are left out — omitted, not hidden.

hits.title: The Barrys
hits.text: The 1915 death notice shows she is the same woman as Kathleen above. Withdrawn. Read rows five and seven together. Catherina Maria Sophia Barry died on 30 July 1859. Catherine Maria Sophia Barry was born on 4 August 1859 — five days later , and was given the dead child's name. That name then travelled: to Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen (1891–1946) , and to Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen (1929–2013) , David Defranceski's grandmother. A four-year-old's death in Burgersdorp is still being commemorated, unknowingly, four generations later.

hits.title: The cousin marriage
hits.text: George was Kathleen's son. Anna was Hendrik's granddaughter. They were first cousins once removed , and their common ancestors are John Augustus Barry I and Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Mary Kolbe . What follows from it Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen descends from John Augustus Barry I and Margaretha Kolbe twice — once through her father, once through her mother. This is pedigree collapse : she has fewer distinct ancestors than the arithmetic of generations predicts. Where a person five generations back should have thirty-two separate ancestors, she has thirty — because one couple occupies two of the slots.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: There is no photograph of their farm, and this archive does not invent one. This archive was built for David Defranceski , born in Johannesburg, living in Brisbane. It runs backwards from his grandmother Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen (1929–2013) — who married Nuno Fernando Lerena at St Joseph's, Mayfair, in 1949 — into the north-eastern Cape: to Barkly East and Dordrecht , to Cradock and Graaff-Reinet , and out again to Württemberg , to Soho , and to a County Cork that may or may not be real. It is a public archive with one rule: the living are left out — omitted, not hidden. And a second rule, which is harder: every claim says how well it is known.

david-schalk-booysen.r: PRISONER OF WAR. A printed transport list in the Pretoria government archives, image group 008019246, carries THREE CONSECUTIVE BOOYZENS shipped on the CITY OF CAMBRIDGE on 3 JUNE 1901, all entered from PRETORIA: 18463 STEPHANUS FRANCOIS, 28 · 18464 PETRUS JACOBUS, 29 · 18465 DAVID SCHALK, 54. Consecutive numbers on one transport means taken together. Age 54 against a birth of 9 June 1848, which would have made him 52 and six days short of 53 when the ship sailed. THE FULLER REGISTER WAS THEN FOUND, and it is better than the De List in every respect: item 1 of the same film, image 126, gives all three as living at PRETORIA, riding with the PRETORIA COMMANDO, and TAKEN AT TOLOSBERG ON 25 APRIL 1901. Its ages are 26, 27 and 53, which match this archive's own dates where the De List's 28, 29 and 54 did not. If it is him, he was a Transvaal burgher in arms at fifty-two, taken and deported, and he came back — he remarried at Pretoria in November 1905. Fourth on the 1863 list, and THE DIRECT ANCESTOR'S BROTHER — Willem Hermanus is sixth on the same list. For the whole of this project he was a line on that list and nothing else. His wife's 1900 death notice gives him a household: married ELIZABETHA MARGARETHA MARAIS at LADY GREY, the same small Cape church where his brother married Kathleen Barry in 1879; eight children; and by 1900 he was at Pretoria, living in a zinc building in Market Street. He signed her notice there in March 1904 — and on 27 NOVEMBER 1905 he married again at Pretoria, to JOHANNA ELENA STOLS, widow Lowies, of Skinners Court. He was 56, a widower of GOEDE HOOP, PRETORIA, and the register gives his birthplace as CRADOCK. The Remarks column cites his remarriage certificate from the Master, NO. 4795 — which is the number of his first wife’s death notice, so the two documents point at each other and the identification needs no inference. His own death is still not found.
p: A zinc building in Market Street

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: The folios followed, into a Pretoria transfer register · Method The land-index folios led to RAK 2384, a deeds transfer register for Wonderboom South — Pretoria, the district where David Schalk Booysen was living when he remarried in 1905. Three rows on one page carry the name, and the household reads Petrus Jacobus, David Schalk, Magdalena Johanna: this archive's direct line, name for name. One row transfers land to a DAVID SCHALK BOOYZEN on 9 April 1907, which would be seventeen months later than anything else held for the man of that name.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: 1900 · A zinc building in Market Street, Pretoria — and the direct line’s own brother A run of ten index entries under Booijzen in the Transvaal probate records carried no dates, no places and nothing to identify them. They all belong to one death notice , and it opens a household this archive did not have: the family of David Schalk Booysen , born 9 June 1848 — the brother of the direct ancestor . Death Notice 4795 , filed 18 March 1904 and stamped by the Master of the Supreme Court, Transvaal, on 2 May 1904 — nearly four years after the death . Under The Administration of Estates Proclamation, 1902 : the proclamation did not exist when she died. The form, as completed 1. Name Elizabetha Margaretha Booijzen (born Marais) 2.

johanna-elena-stols.r: His second wife, married at Pretoria on 27 November 1905 — she 51 and a WIDOW LOWIES of Skinners Court, he 56 and a widower of Goede Hoop. Her first husband was CHARLES PETRUS BAREND LOWIES, born in the district of Cradock about 1849 and dead at Pretoria on 5 JUNE 1905 — FIVE MONTHS AND TWENTY-TWO DAYS before she married again. Estate 7081, which the marriage register cites beside his 4795. TWELVE children by Lowies, SIX OF THEM STILL MINORS when he died — and her second husband lived at the same address, GOEDEHOOP. She signed her first husband’s death notice on 27 October 1905 and married her second on 27 November.

charles-petrus-barend-lowies.r: Her first husband, and estate 7081 — the OTHER number cited in the Remarks column of the 1905 marriage register. Born in the district of CRADOCK about 1849, within a year of David Schalk Booysen and in the same Karoo district; dead at Pretoria, where David Schalk had been widowed five years earlier. His parents were JAN LOWIES and ELISABETHA MARIA LUBBE, and he left TWELVE children. THE FILE IS NOW READ. He was a HAWKER, of GOEDEHOOP, PRETORIA — which is the exact address David Schalk Booyzen gave on the marriage register three weeks later, so the two men lived in the same place. Dutch, of the Cradock district, 56 years and 8 months, dead in the LUNATIC ASYLUM at Pretoria on 5 June 1905. Movables but no land, an estate over £100, and a will. Six of the twelve children were still minors. His widow signed the notice on 27 October and married David Schalk on 27 November.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: 7081 is the bride's, and it is CHARLES PETRUS BAREND LOWIES — born in the DISTRICT OF CRADOCK about 1849, dead at PRETORIA on 5 JUNE 1905, parents Jan Lowies and Elisabetha Maria Lubbe, TWELVE children. Read the two men together: David Schalk Booijzen born Cradock 9 June 1848 and widowed at Pretoria in 1900; Charles Petrus Barend Lowies born district Cradock about 1849 and dead at Pretoria in 1905. Two men born a year apart in one Karoo district, both ending in Pretoria — and five months and twenty-two days after the second died, the first married his widow. The Master cleared both estates within four days: 4795 on 4 November, 7081 on the 7th, the wedding on the 27th.

hits.text: 4795 was David Schalk’s and led back to his first wife’s death notice. This is 7081 , read entire — and it is not the document this archive expected. elizabetha-margaretha-marais.r: His wife, married at Lady Grey near Aliwal North. Daughter of STEPHANUS FRANCOIS MARAIS and ELIZABETHA MARGARETHA MARAIS, born in the district of Cradock about April 1850. She died in a ZINC BUILDING IN MARKET STREET, PRETORIA on 1 June 1900 — four days before Lord Roberts entered the town — and her husband did not file the notice for three years and nine months. Nothing movable left, and a compensation claim filed.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: The dates here make it unmistakable, and this archive keeps the two apart. Five of the eight children of that marriage are named for a parent or a grandparent — the same habit as the Barry names crossing into the Daschners, seen from the other direction and in another family. Johanna Catharina Booysen gets her dates · Found Second on the 1863 death notice and until now nothing but a position in a list. The Dutch Reformed index gives her born 15 May 1844 and baptised at BRAK RIVIER on 4 August 1844 — the farm her father was still on nineteen years later when her mother died there. A small thing, and the kind the register was built to hand over.

johanna-booyzen.r: NOT THIS FAMILY, and recorded here on purpose. Death notice 6167 — the oldest Booyzen estate paper in the Cape Master's series, and a generation older in form than anything else this archive has read. Widow of Charles du Plessis; one daughter, married to Benjamin Solomon; “no property whatever except a Bond amounting per balance to £15”. Line 3 answers “both dead”. She is here because she was born in 1754 and died in 1843 — the only two dates this archive has for Magdelena Elisabeth de Beer, both off the family tree with no source stated — and because somebody will one day find her and decide she is the same woman. She is not. Her name is not Magdelena, not Elisabeth, and not de Beer.

willem-hermanus-booyzen-of-indwe.v: Booijzen (1907 lidmate register) · William Hermanus (1908 marriage) · William Herman Booyzen (1932)
willem-hermanus-booyzen-of-indwe.d: 29 Jul 1932, Johannesburg Hospital — buried Brixton, grave 6889
willem-hermanus-booyzen-of-indwe.r: AN EIGHTH CHILD, and one this archive did not have. Confirmed at Indwe on 31 May 1907, aged 21, entered “Booijzen”. A MIJNWERKER of DUGMORE MIJN when he married Susanna Adriana Roodt, 16, at Indwe on 21 September 1908 — the only miner in five generations of read occupations, and the answer to the last line of the family testimony. Two children in nine months by two women of the same surname, both entered “onecht”. His mother stood godmother at the first font, which is how this archive knows whose son he is. AND THEN JOHANNESBURG: a WILLIAM HERMAN BOOYZEN, 47, born Cape Province, married, EX MINER UNDERGROUND, of 62 Langford Street, Booysens, died at Johannesburg Hospital on 29 July 1932 of a perforated duodenal ulcer after about one day, and was buried at BRIXTON on 31 July. The occupation, the province, the age within a year and the cemetery all fit; no parents are named, because a civil registration does not ask. And then the grave register closes it: GRAVE 6889 holds “Boysen, William” and, thirty-six years later, SUSANNA ADRIANA BOOYZEN, buried 29 August 1968 — the woman he married at Indwe in 1908. hits.title: The name
hits.text: 1899 — with the diaeresis, the older Cape Dutch orthography, in the year the war began Kolbe-Booysen a compound recorded for Maria Jacoba Smit, who married David Kolbe Booyzen in 1921 Within a single sibling group the tree records Jacobus Nicolaas Booysen (b. 1840) and Jacobus Nicolaas Booyzen (b. 1841), both dying on 17 November 1882 . That is almost certainly one man entered twice under two spellings — a small demonstration of how easily this name splits.

henry-james-booyzen.d: 8 Dec 1956, Florence Nightingale Nursing Home — buried 12 Dec, grave 7110/1
henry-james-booyzen.r: A son of Willem Hermanus and Kathleen Barry. WikiTree gives his birth as 12 AUGUST 1887 and his marriage as 17 JUNE 1912 AT ELLIOT, neither of which this archive had—bothFROM WIKITREE, NOT FROM A DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS READ, and the “c. 1887” below is this archive’s own figure, worked back from an age on a burial register. This archive had him as a name on Transvaal estate MHG 10/57 and nothing else — not a birth, not a death. The Johannesburg cemetery register gives all of it: DIED 8 DECEMBER 1956 at the FLORENCE NIGHTINGALE NURSING HOME of CORONARY PULMONARY SCLEROSIS, aged 69, usual residence 3 15TH AVENUE, MAYFAIR — the same suburb where his mother died in 1940 and where his great-niece was married at St Joseph’s in 1949. Buried 12 December in the D.R. section, GRAVE 7110/1, a double plot. In 1912 he married Dorothea Regina Barry, a daughter of his mother's brother Hendrik Nicholaas — the third Barry–Booyzen union in three generations.

richard-peter-booyzen.d: 25 Oct 1918, Turffontein — buried 27 Oct, Brixton, D.R., grave 1119
richard-peter-booyzen.r: TWENTY-FOUR, MARRIED, a SAWYER of 18 Anderson Street, Turffontein — dead of INFLUENZA AND PNEUMONIA after eleven days on 25 October 1918, the centre of Black October, and buried at Brixton on the 27th. Not in this archive before today. Added as a ninth child of Willem Hermanus and Kathleen Barry on three grounds and no document: RICHARD PETER is her own brother's name; a birth about 1894 falls exactly in the gap between her daughter of 1891 and her son of 1901; and his registration gives his birthplace as the CAPE OF GOOD HOPE, which is the migration every one of her children made. A Transvaal death registration names no parents, so this stays INFERRED. And he was NOT A SOLDIER — which kills the best explanation this archive had for his mother's military pension.

This archive has no Richard Peter Booyzen and it should: Richard Peter Barry is Kathleen's own brother, and a boy born about 1894 falls exactly in the gap between her daughter of 1891 and her son of 1901. Added as a ninth child, marked INFERRED, because a burial register names no parents. Two more Booysens went into the same ground within eight weeks and neither can be shown to be kin.

hits.text: Born Cape Province. Indwe. Married. Since 1908. Forty-seven in July 1932 against twenty-two in September 1908 — which makes him forty-six. One year. Brixton Cemetery, 31 July 1932 , where the burial register gives his birth as 1885 and where this family already buries its Johannesburg dead: Anna J. Mary Booyzen in 1914, John Barry Booyzen in 1916, George Downing Daschner in 1925. And “Sasanna Adriana Booyzen” was buried at Johannesburg in 1968 — his widow, under his name, thirty-six years after him. What does not No parents are named , because a South African civil death registration does not ask for them unless the deceased is under ten.

catharina-maria-sophia-booysen.d: 1946 — West Park, grave 51, beside her husband
catharina-maria-sophia-booysen.r: Baptised at Barkly Oost 24 May 1891, entry 120, named for her mother entire, and fourteen when her father died at Indwe. She married Joseph Heinrich Daschner AT INDWE — the same village — and his 1942 death notice names her “born Booyzen”, with a z, in a Johannesburg typist’s hands. Eleven children, five of them carrying Booyzen and Barry forenames. She died in the Transvaal in 1946 — estate TAB MHG 3734/46, found only when this archive finally searched outside the Cape, and still to be read.

hits.title: The Barrys
hits.text: It does not prove the rebel is Kathleen's brother. It does show that whoever named this child was standing inside the same family this archive is describing. The namesakes → How far the Barry names travel There is no Barry surname left in this family after 1859. There is a great deal of Barry name . The children of Catharina Maria Sophia Booysen — Kathleen Barry's daughter — on her husband's 1942 death notice. Kathleen Barry married a Booyzen in the 1880s, so the surname stops with her. Her daughter married a Daschner, so it is two surnames gone in two generations.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: And a DOUBLE PLOT: Joseph Heinrich Daschner, 58, buried 21 April 1942 in GRAVE 50 of a pair 50/51 he bought himself, with a memorial by L. Canata & Son — and the consecutive grave-number register braces 50 and 51 together, DASCHNER JOSEPH H. and DASCHNER CATHERINE M.S. She is Catharina Maria Sophia Booysen, born 22 April 1891 at Barkly Oost, George's own sister, whose estate MHG 3734/46 is one of the six files in the letter to Pretoria. Four years after he was buried in the first grave she went into the second.

And a sixth, off the 1942 list The Johannesburg cemetery index carries a George Downing Daschner , buried at Brixton on 20 June 1925, the year he was born. He is not on his father's death notice because he was dead seventeen years before it was written — a twelfth child. George Downing is the name of Kathleen Barry's own grandson, born in 1901, and here it is on an infant in another family in the same decade. A second of the name died in 1998.

stephanus-francois-booyzen.r: PRISONER OF WAR. A printed transport list in the Pretoria government archives, image group 008019246, carries THREE CONSECUTIVE BOOYZENS shipped on the CITY OF CAMBRIDGE on 3 JUNE 1901, all entered from PRETORIA: 18463 STEPHANUS FRANCOIS, 28 · 18464 PETRUS JACOBUS, 29 · 18465 DAVID SCHALK, 54. Consecutive numbers on one transport means taken together. Age 28 against this archive's c. October 1874, which would have made him 26. THE FULLER REGISTER WAS THEN FOUND, and it is better than the De List in every respect: item 1 of the same film, image 126, gives all three as living at PRETORIA, riding with the PRETORIA COMMANDO, and TAKEN AT TOLOSBERG ON 25 APRIL 1901. Its ages are 26, 27 and 53, which match this archive's own dates where the De List's 28, 29 and 54 did not. AND THEN THE PRISONER NUMBER LED SOMEWHERE ELSE ENTIRELY. The medal-roll database at angloboerwar.com holds an entry for a STEPHANUS FRANCOIS BOOYSEN, BURGER, whose PoW number is 18463 — the same number as the register — and it says he was a ZARP, one of the ZAR's police, based at PRETORIA. Quoting a City Coins auction catalogue of November 2020 that described his ABO medal and the papers with it: in action at TALANA, MODDER SPRUIT, COLENSO, PLATRAND (WAGON HILL) where he was WOUNDED IN THE RIGHT LEG ABOVE THE KNEE, SPION KOP and DALMANUTHA — the ZARPs' famous last stand. His applications were completed by his commanding officer, COMMANDANT J. P. DE LA C. SCHROEDER. He was one of FORTY-TWO Boers taken at Tolosberg in the Waterval Valley on 25 April 1901, with two guns and much stock, and was sent to INDIA. This archive has NOT seen the medal or the application; it is strong secondary evidence tied to the register by the number and not by the name. WHAT IT DOES TO THE DISPUTE: he is numbered 18463 and David Schalk Booysen is 18465, two apart on the same transport on the same day, and this man died at EAST LYNNE, PRETORIA, which is the district all three were taken in. That is a FOURTH point favouring David Schalk as his father, and the first that does not depend on a forename. It is still not a document naming a parent. PARENTAGE DISPUTED — see below. A son of the second marriage, and a MESSELAAR — a mason, like his half-brother Willem Hermanus at Indwe. His 1940 Sterfkennis was fetched because it should have named his mother; his widow wrote only “oorlede” for both parents. Married BEATRIX MAGDALENA CATHARINA BOSHOFF at Mosselbaai on 5 SEPTEMBER 1905, certificate 1318 — he 30 and a JONKMAN, she SIXTEEN with her parents consenting. Eleven children; left immovable property and a will. THE REGISTER GIVES HIS RESIDENCE AS PRETORIA, and eleven weeks later David Schalk Booijzen of Goede Hoop, Pretoria — whose 1900 notice names an unmarried major son called Stephanus François — remarried in that same city. This archive placed him under Petrus Jacobus on his birth year alone. It is marked SERIOUS on the disputed page and it is not decided.

hits.text: If Stephanus Francois is David Schalk Booijzen's son, as the 1900 Pretoria death notice says, that boy carries his grandfather's name outright; under the parentage this archive published instead, he carries a great-uncle's. A third point for the new reading, and still not proof. Added to the disputed row, which stays Serious. hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Eight columns — and none of them asks where anybody was born, which is the whole difficulty. Entry 1318 , Duplicaat Origineel Register , Mosselbaai, 5 September 1905 . What the register gives Stefanus Francois Booyzen , 30 , JONKMAN — a bachelor — METSELAAR , a mason, woonplaats tijdens het huwelijk: PRETORIA . He married Beatrix Magdalena Catharina Boshoff , 16 , jongdochter of Mosselbaai, with her ouders consenting, in the N.G. Kerk by John Murray . What it does not give No parents. No birthplace. This register has a column for woonplaats tijdens het huwelijk and none for waar geboren — unlike the Zeerust register of 1892, which gave this archive Hendrik Stefanus’s Graaff-Reinet. The question is not settled and this document cannot settle it.

david-schalk-booyzen-of-1940.r: Eldest named on his father's 1940 estate — and a name that matters. If Stephanus Francois is DAVID SCHALK BOOIJZEN's son, as the 1900 death notice suggests, then this boy is called after his grandfather outright. Under the reading this archive published instead, he is called after a great-uncle. It is a point in the argument and not a proof.

hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: If he is David Schalk Booijzen’s son, that boy is called after his grandfather outright; under the reading this archive published, he is called after a great-uncle. Two of the eleven — Ewert Philippus and Susanna Fredrika Aletta — are called straight after his WIFE’S parents, Evert Philip Boshoff and Susanna Frederika Aletta Meyer, which shows this couple did name children after grandparents. The naming argues for the new reading: her father was STEPHANUS FRANCOIS MARAIS, which is exactly where the forename would come from, and there is no Stephanus Francois anywhere in the Pretorius side.

hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: If he is David Schalk Booijzen’s son, that boy is called after his grandfather outright; under the reading this archive published, he is called after a great-uncle. Two of the eleven — Ewert Philippus and Susanna Fredrika Aletta — are called straight after his WIFE’S parents, Evert Philip Boshoff and Susanna Frederika Aletta Meyer, which shows this couple did name children after grandparents. The naming argues for the new reading: her father was STEPHANUS FRANCOIS MARAIS, which is exactly where the forename would come from, and there is no Stephanus Francois anywhere in the Pretorius side.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: The form did not change. The person filling it in did. Her husband signed it, and her parents were alive and reachable. Withdrawn — Maggie born 1 October 1926 · Taken back This archive carried Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth “Maggie” Booyzen’s birth as 1 October 1926, taken from the family tree. Her mother’s 1944 death notice, written and signed by her father three months before he lost her, gives 14 October 1926. Every other child’s date on that list matches what the archive already held, which is what makes the one mismatch worth taking seriously. Corrected to 14 October.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: Both of them lie under a cut-stone monument at Burgersdorp — names, London birthplaces, farm and dates carved into it — about forty miles from where that notice was written. The family forgot them inside seventy years, with the headstone still standing. And it had happened before, on the other side of the house. In 1840 a relative of James Montjoy filled in the same printed form at the same box. He knew the dead man's trade, his house, what it was worth, the village he died in and the name of his wife's first husband. Where it asked for the parents, he wrote: "Names of the Parents of the Deceased. Not Known ." — and for birth-place, only "Europe" . James Montjoy had died thirteen years earlier .

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: So of the three figures the archive had, the marriage register is the outlier : it gives his age as 22 in December 1879, when he was 28 . His 1905 death registration says 55 , which is right within a year. The 1879 entry is wrong by six years. And he was named for his godfather The witnesses are Willem Hermanus Pieterzen , Maria Catharina Magdalena Potgieter and Xaverius Hermanus Pieterzen . (The archive scan corrects this archive's earlier reading of the surname as Pietersen — see below; the first given name, earlier read as Iwerus , is still not certain.) Johanna Catharina Mountjoy's half-brothers were Pieterzens — the sons of Anna Catharina Sleer by her first marriage.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: A third indexing, under the spelling Montyoy , did. Graaff-Reinet marriage register, folios 60–61. "Den 9 Maart 1817 getrouwd" — married on 9 March 1817. The entry, with a pencil cross beside it: "James Montjoy — Met · Anna Catharina Slier, weduwe van Harmanus Pieterze[n]" What it does not say, and that is the point This archive went to this register expecting an origin . Cape marriage entries of this date routinely record where a party came from, and this very page does it repeatedly — three couples in the right-hand column are entered "beide van Uitenhage" . Against James Montjoy's name there is a long ruled dash and nothing else .

hits.title: The namesakes
hits.text: Five generations, and it does not come from this family at all Willem Hermanus The name enters through a step-relation with no blood tie to any Booyzen, and is still being given to children a century and a half later. Who When What they are to the name Willem Hermanus Pieterzen d. bef. 1817 Anna Catharina Slier's FIRST husband. Not a Booyzen, not a Mountjoy, and no blood relation to either. Willem Hermanus Pieterzen the son His son by her, and godfather at the 1851 Graaff-Reinet font — half-brother to Johanna Catharina Mountjoy. Willem Hermanus “William Henry” Booyzen 1851–1905 Named at that font for the godfather standing over it. Generation four of the direct line.

hits.title: The namesakes
hits.text: Willem Hermanus “Willy” Booyzen 1925–1996 Eldest of the Johannesburg family. William Herman Daschner b. c. 1915 And out through a daughter into a third surname. This archive published “Willem Hermanus is a Booyzen name” and withdrew it. Three documents name the first husband three ways — Harmanus Pieterze in 1817, William Pietersen in 1840, Willem Hermanus Pieterzen in 1851 — and the man they name married into the line and died before it started. Five generations of women, across four surnames — and it is not a Barry name Catherine Maria Sophia This archive called it “a Barry name that outlives the Barry surname by eighty years”.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Johanna Catharina was eight — her own 1863 death notice puts her birth at 30 April 1819. Jacoba was seven, George four, James one. And Thomas Jacobus , born 1818, is not on the list — which independently supports the correction that he died in 1827 rather than in infancy in 1818. A correction the tree needs Our tree records James Mountjoy as born and died in 1826 . He is listed here alive, as a minor , at his father's death in September 1827. The infant-death date is wrong. Where the line now ends, and why it is a real end. James Montjoy, a saddler born in "Europe" about 1782, who owned a house and erf at Cradock worth £90 and died there in September 1827 leaving four children under nine.

hits.title: Open questions
hits.text: Here are three named Mountjoys in the right district, twenty-six years after her death. Answered They are the descendants of Johanna Catharina Mountjoy's brother. George Mountjoy (b. 1823, Cradock), saddle maker , married Maria Sophia Botha at Cradock in 1848 and had thirteen children. Hercules Johannes (the father at the 1889 font) and James/Jakobus Jonathan (the witness, who died at Barkly East in 1937) are two of his sons. The child baptised that day, George Mountjoy (1889–1963) , was a second cousin of the Booyzen daughter baptised in the same register three weeks earlier.

hits.text: One of them was accumulating and one of them was not. The line → 1902 · A wrong name in the index, and a right family behind it Searching the Cape probate index for Hercules Johannes Mountjoy returns exactly one hit. It is not his. Kennisgeving van Sterfgeval , filed 3 January 1903. Carolina Deybella Margrietta Alletta van Niekerk, geboren Botha , died at her own house at Dordrecht , 18 December 1902. Why it comes up Because his name is written on it. Fifth in her list of eleven children: "5. Maria Sophia van Niekerk, getrouwd met Hercules Johannes Mountjoy." The FamilySearch index keys every name on the page , so a search hit is not a statement about whose document it is.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: So the van Niekerks are now documented. Maria Sophia van Niekerk , who married Hercules Johannes Mountjoy at Dordrecht on 8 October 1888, was a daughter of Jan Dirk Abram Frans van Niekerk and Carolina Deybella Margrietta Alletta Botha , who was herself born in the district of Cradock and whose parents were Philip Rudolph Botha and a mother of the same long name. Her ten brothers and sisters were Carolina Deybella Margrietta Alletta, Cornelius, Maria Francina Cecilia (widow of Gert Olivier), Jan Dirk Abram Frans, Hercules Johannes , Christiaan Jacobus, Cornelia Elizabeth Gertruida (married James Ross), Benjamin Jacobus, Pieter Jacobus and Philip Rudolph.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: She died at Wodehouse on 25 October 1897, aged fourteen months. On 8 November 1901 they had another daughter and gave her the whole name again; she married Hendrik Stefanus Palm, and a granddaughter born in 1920 carries it still. Replacement naming is well attested in these congregations and is exactly how a records-matcher invents one person out of two. The dates here make it unmistakable, and this archive keeps the two apart.

john-barry.r: One profile holding two men — and on 14 September 2026 they came apart. THE YORKSHIRE MAN IS NOW A LIFE: born at WHITBY in 1796; resident at BILSDALE MIDCABLE when he took a licence on 2 October 1838 to marry MARGARET JACKSON of Beadlam at Helmsley; and in the 1851 census a SHIP OWNER at SHIP YARDS, RUSWARP, WHITBY, aged 55, married, head of his household — the ONLY John Barry of that age in the whole Yorkshire census. John Barry deaths are then registered in the WHITBY district in 1858 and in 1860. He outlived the Cape man, who died at de Bruins Poort in 1853, by at least five years. THEY ARE TWO MEN. What this archive still does not have is the Cape one: no birth, no arrival, no burial. And a caution worth keeping — a Whitby SHIP OWNER is exactly the kind of man whose son could be born AT SEA, which is what John Augustus Barry's death notice says of 1819. That coincidence is not evidence, and the censuses say it is not the same man.

hits.title: The cousin marriage
hits.text: The Schoemans sit alongside the Barrys in the same way. P. Schoeman witnessed the 1879 Booysen–Barry marriage ; Anna Johanna Maria Schoemann married Hendrik Nicholaas Barry in 1877; and the 1901 Pretorius–Barry wedding was held at the home of D. Schoeman . Why that matters → The names give it away Anna's mother was christened Margarietha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Barry — the same four names, in the same order, as her own grandmother Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Mary Kolbe . And Anna herself was "named after Anna Johanna Maria Schoemann" , her father's mother, a fact the tree records explicitly rather than leaving to be inferred.

james-henry-barry.v: Henry Jaonas Barry · Hennery James Berry (both 1848 index entries)
james-henry-barry.r: SETTLED, 14 September 2026, and it removes a candidate rather than adding one. The HENRY JAONAS BARRY who turned up on 13 September — “baptised at twenty years old” in 1868, and briefly a candidate for a tenth child — IS THIS MAN. The same event is indexed twice: once as Henry Jaonas Barry, baptism 13 Nov 1868, and once as HENNERY JAMES BERRY, baptism 13 Nov 1848. Same birth date of 13 July 1848, same parents, same collection, and FamilySearch attaches BOTH to one tree person, James Henry Barry 1848–1939. The volume decides the year on its own: the register is “GRAAFF-REINET. BAPTISM RECORDS 1846–1851”, and a baptism of 1868 cannot sit in a book that closes in 1851. So he was baptised at four months, not at twenty, AT GRAAFF-REINET — not at Cape Town or Tulbagh, which is what both index entries say for the place. The birth-spacing argument made against him held: his brother John Augustus II was born 13 March 1847 and he was born sixteen months later. THE IMAGE HAS BEEN LOCATED AND NOT READ — identifier apid:TH-909-70517-31299-17. Named on the 1915 death notice, which he swore himself. The index now dates him: born about 1847, dead at Barkly East on 23 June 1939, having outlived his father by thirty-six years. BUT THAT YEAR CANNOT STAND. His brother John Augustus Barry II was born 13 MARCH 1847 off a register, and “about 1847” here is not a date at all — it is an age worked back from the 1939 death. Two brothers cannot share it. A relationship search on his mother's surname turned up a HENRY JAONAS BARRY born 13 July 1848 and baptised at twenty, which is where a next child belongs; whether that is this man under a clerk's ear is UNPROVED and the register is unread.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Catherine Mary Sophia is her own name, and her mother's before her — Kathleen Barry , born 1859. Margaret Wilhelmina Elizabeth is the Barry name that runs down the other side of this family too. William Herman is Willem Hermanus , her father. Richard Peter is her uncle, Richard Peter Barry . Henry James is her brother. Five of eleven Daschner children carry Booyzen and Barry names. The surname leaves the family in one generation. The names do not. This is the same evidence the archive uses on the name and in the cousin marriage : in this family, forenames are inherited property, and they travel through daughters as reliably as surnames travel through sons.

william-henry-keys.r: Married JOHANNA CATHARINA MOUNTJOY, baptised at Burgersdorp on 29 February 1860 — a daughter of George Mountjoy and Maria Sophia Botha, which this archive had been asking about and can now answer. Eight children baptised across Dordrecht, Barkly East and Barkly West between 1878 and 1898: Robert Byron, William Henry, JAMES JONATHAN, George, Lancelott Byron, Cecil Frederik, Rachel Anna Maria and HERKLAAS EDWARD JOHANNES. The Mountjoy forenames crossing into a third surname, exactly as the Barry names crossed into the Daschners — and BYRON twice, which appears nowhere else in this archive.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: And the Keys question is answered. This site has carried a William Henry Keys who married a Johanna Catharina Mountjoy and baptised children at Dordrecht, Burgersdorp and Barkly East between 1878 and 1898 — among them James Jonathan Keys and Herklaas Edward Johannes Keys , Mountjoy forenames crossing into a third surname. It has been asking which Johanna Catharina Mountjoy. This one. The Keys marriage record estimates her birth at 1859 ; the Burgersdorp font gives 28 January 1860 . She is George Mountjoy’s daughter , and the Mountjoy forenames that turn up in the Keys children are her father’s and her brother’s.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: And the Keys question is answered. This site has carried a William Henry Keys who married a Johanna Catharina Mountjoy and baptised children at Dordrecht, Burgersdorp and Barkly East between 1878 and 1898 — among them James Jonathan Keys and Herklaas Edward Johannes Keys , Mountjoy forenames crossing into a third surname. It has been asking which Johanna Catharina Mountjoy. This one. The Keys marriage record estimates her birth at 1859 ; the Burgersdorp font gives 28 January 1860 . She is George Mountjoy’s daughter , and the Mountjoy forenames that turn up in the Keys children are her father’s and her brother’s.

hits.title: The Barrys
hits.text: A second of the name died in 1998. This comes from an index and not from an image, and the page says so. But it moves the reading: six names, not five , and a pattern that cannot comfortably be called coincidence. The namesakes → This matters to the rebel question in a small, real way. When the Cape Rebel roll produces a Fred J. Barry of Ivanhoe and a Richard Peter Barry of Jerpoint, the second name is not a coincidence to be waved at — it is a name this family demonstrably used and kept using. It still does not prove the man on the roll is Kathleen's brother, and this archive still marks that unproven . But it does mean the name is evidence of a family, not of an individual.

hits.title: The Kolbes
hits.text: They read exactly as a missionary's children's names should: scriptural, Latinate, chosen rather than inherited. And one of them travels. Frederik Fortunatus Kolbe (1839) becomes Frederick Fortunatus Barry (1863) becomes Frederik Fortsenatus Booÿsen (1899) — one name carried across three surnames and sixty years, degrading slightly at each handover. The women → John Gottlob Kolbe, 1765–1845 — a tailor of Bond Street The tree leads with the German original, Johan Gottlieb .

hits.title: The namesakes
hits.text: This archive keeps the two apart, and says which is which. One name, three surnames, no blood tie proved between two of them Fortunatus It comes out of the London Kolbes and ends up on a Booÿsen born in the year the war began. Who When What they are to the name Frederik Fortunatus Kolbe of the London Kolbes The source of the name. Frederick Fortunatus Barry — Carried into the Barrys by the Kolbe marriage of 1850. Frederik Fortsenatus Booÿsen b. 1899 And into the Booysens, spelled with a diaeresis, in 1899. Ruben, a Schoeman name, travels the same way into the Barrys — Ruben Jacobus Josuah Barry. Two daughters, one name, eleven months apart The two Gertrudes Not a duplicated record. Two children, two death certificates, two cemeteries.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: The route is closed for a demonstrable reason, and what remains is the registers themselves, read across the gaps. Two fonts, a year apart, and every witness a Kolbe · Found Having read one Barry baptism, the one before it was worth reading too. At the 1847 font the witnesses are John Kolbe, Margaret Kolbe and Augusta Kolbe; at the 1848 font, Catharine Sophia Maria Kolbe. Two children, two years, and not a Barry witness between them. That is the same conclusion the namesake correction reached from one entry, arrived at a second time from another — the names this archive has called Barry names belong to the people who stood at the fonts, and they were all Kolbes.

catharine-sophia-maria-kolbe.v: Catharine Kolbe (1853) · Catharine Sophia Maria Kolber (1848)
catharine-sophia-maria-kolbe.r: SHE IS WHERE THE NAME COMES FROM, and this archive had her down as “Catharine Kolbe” and nothing more. On 13 November 1848 she stood godmother at Graaff-Reinet to her sister Margaretha's son HENRY JAMES BARRY, entry 603, and the clerk wrote her out in full: CATHARINE SOPHIA MARIA KOLBER. ELEVEN YEARS LATER her sister named a daughter CATHERINE MARIA SOPHIA — the Kathleen Barry who married into this family — and the name then ran through four more generations and three more surnames. This archive had called it a Barry name. It is a Kolbe name, and it belongs to a woman who never married into the Booyzens at all. She is also godmother at Burgersdorp in 1853, two entries above her sister Mary Elizabeth's son.

hits.text: Two fonts, a year apart, and every witness a Kolbe · Found Having read one Barry baptism, the one before it was worth reading too. At the 1847 font the witnesses are John Kolbe, Margaret Kolbe and Augusta Kolbe; at the 1848 font, Catharine Sophia Maria Kolbe. Two children, two years, and not a Barry witness between them. That is the same conclusion the namesake correction reached from one entry, arrived at a second time from another — the names this archive has called Barry names belong to the people who stood at the fonts, and they were all Kolbes.

The 1848 font says otherwise: it is a KOLBE name, and the woman it comes from never married a Booyzen. Who When What they are to the name Catharine Sophia Maria Kolbe godmother, 1848 Stood at the Graaff-Reinet font on 13 November 1848 for her sister's son Henry James Barry, entry 603, written out in full by the clerk. hits.text: A three-way agreement, which in this archive is rare enough to be worth stating. And it settles the Enslin problem. mary-elizabeth-kolbe.r: MARGARETHA'S SISTER, and the woman who married GEORGE FREDERICK ENSLIN — which is the whole answer to a contradiction this archive carried as Serious, that Margaretha appeared to marry Enslin while married to John Barry. It was resolved from Margaret Downing's 1867 death notice. The Burgersdorp register of 23 October 1853 shows it instead: the two sisters baptising a son each, two entries apart, on one page.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: It was resolved from Margaret Downing’s 1867 death notice , which lists among her children “Mary Elizabeth (dead) who was married to George F. Enslin” . The Enslin marriage belongs to Margaretha’s sister . Here are the two sisters, on one page, on one day, baptising a son each. Mary Elizabeth Kolbe with her Enslin, Margareth Kolbe with her Barry, two entries apart in the Burgersdorp register on 23 October 1853. The contradiction → And it puts them at Burgersdorp. The 1915 death notice says the marriage was at “Burghersdorp (probably)” — a son guessing, sixty-five years on, at something nobody had told him.

anna-van-der-merwe-of-burgersdorp.r: The third godparent at the 1853 Barry font, and the only one who is not a Kolbe. A VAN DER MERWE standing at a Barry christening at Burgersdorp — a surname this archive has been chasing on the entirely other side of the family, among the Booysens of Graaff-Reinet. Not connected, and set down so the coincidence is on the record.

william-barry.r: Found twice in one day. He came in on the 1915 death notice of his mother Margaretha Kolbe, estate 1291, which names NINE children where his father's names eight — and then the Burgersdorp doopregister produced his baptism: WILLIAM FREDRIK, born 23 August 1853, christened 23 October, godparents JOHN KOLBE, ANNA VAN DER MERWE and GEORGE KOLBE. Two of the three are his mother's brothers. A SECOND William Frederick Thomas was baptised in 1861 and this archive cannot say whether the first died or a clerk erred — a doubt re-surfaced, and briefly mistaken for a new find, when the index was asked for every Barry child of a Kolbe mother. He is not on his father's notice, not on the Cape Rebel roll, and nowhere else in this archive. hits.text: His own documents call him simply John Barry, and that is the third man in this family the name has to be shared out between. His birth date does one more job than it looks: being HARD, off a register, it is what forces his brother James Henry's “about 1847” to move. Read beside his brother’s font of the following year, where the godmother is CATHARINE SOPHIA MARIA KOLBER, it makes one point twice: the forenames this archive has spent the project calling BARRY NAMES are Kolbe names, standing at Kolbe godparents’ fonts. He remains exactly what he was: an unresolved second William, indexed twice over to Graaff-Reinet and Dordrecht , eight years after the Burgersdorp baptism . On Henry Jaonas there is an argument, and it comes entirely out of figures this archive already held. John Augustus Barry II was born 13 March 1847 and baptised four weeks later — a documented date, off a register. James Henry Barry is carried in this archive as born "about 1847" , and that figure is not a register at all: it is an age worked back from his death at Barkly East on 23 June 1939. Two brothers cannot both be born in 1847 , and the approximate date is the one that has to give way.

johan-gottlieb-kolbe.r: AND HE IS IN THE LONDON GAZETTE, nine years before he died: issue 19424, page 1702, 29 September 1836, dissolving the copartnership of “JOHN GOTTLOB KOLBE and DAVID FLETCHER, of Conduit-Street, Bond-Street, in the County of Middlesex, TAILORS”. That is his trade, his street and a business partner, in print, from a free source — and it pushes him back to Conduit Street in 1836. AND THE DEATH IS NOW A GRO REFERENCE: FreeBMD gives one Kolbe death in all of England and Wales for 1845–46 — “Deaths Dec 1845, KOLBE, JOHN GOTTLOB, ST GEO HAN SQ, VOL 1, PAGE 35”. The district matches the census; the name form JOHN GOTTLOB matches his son's 1803 baptism; and the certificate, not yet ordered, would name the informant. FOUND IN THE 1841 CENSUS, which settles two things this archive had argued from other documents. He is at CONDUIT STREET, St George Hanover Square, sub-district MAY FAIR, aged 76 — four years before he died at number 34, and independent of the death record that corrected the family tree's Lamb's Conduit Street. And his birth county is entered as “FOREIGN”, which is the first document in this archive to say in its own words that he was not English. HO107, piece 734, book 1, folio 11, page 15, SCHEDULE 38. Three women share that schedule: Marianne, 35, Charlotte, 30, and Amelia A., 25. Tailor. Died at 34 Conduit Street, Mayfair — not Lamb's Conduit Street; the tree's photograph is of the wrong building. Buried at the German Savoy Church, Strand.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: What this archive has established The letter was changed on purpose Booyzen , not Booysen. The family says the spelling was changed during the Anglo-Boer War, to avoid being taken for men who fought on the British side — and the surname statistics agree with the family. The name → The Kolbes end in London, not the Cape Johan Gottlieb Kolbe died at 34 Conduit Street on 18 November 1845 and was buried at the German Savoy Church eight days later, aged 81. The line runs out of the Cape and into a German congregation in Mayfair. The Kolbes → They married their cousins, and it is documented Not lore: the marriages are on the register, and the archive sets out which couples were related and how closely.

hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: The tree has Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Mary, born Graaff-Reinet. Serious Her mother’s 1867 death notice lists her as “Margaret Wilhelmina, married to J. Barry”, which supports the tree against the 1915 guess. The informant in 1915 did not know his own grandparents’ names, so his accuracy on his mother’s is not to be relied on. → Johan Gottlieb Kolbe — place of burial The tree records “St John the Baptist, Leamington, Warwickshire.” Resolved WRONG. The register reads “St John Baptist, in the GERMAN SAVOY CHURCH, in the County of Middlesex” — the German Lutheran chapel in the Strand, a hundred miles from Warwickshire, and the same congregation that holds five of his children and his wife. Someone matched the dedication to the wrong church.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Movable property: No . Immovable: No . Estate: Nil . No will. She died in her son's house at Manorowen. Set that beside her mother Margaret Downing , who in 1867 left a house in Burgersdorp and a farm in the division of Albert; beside her grandfather Johan Gottlieb Kolbe , whose 1842 will disposed of a partnership in a Bond Street tailoring firm; and beside her husband John Barry , whose estate in 1903 exceeded £300. The Kolbe money did not last three generations. This notice also supplies a third date for John Barry's death — "August 1904" — against the 3 August 1903 of his own 1915 death notice and the 25 August 1903 in the tree.

We have no service number for any son — but we know there was a pension, and we know the pensioner's name, her exact address and her date of death. The pension registers can be searched on those. § 14 · High priority Did any of the Bond Street money reach the Cape? Johan Gottlieb Kolbe's 1842 will divides his residue among his children, with the issue of any dead child taking that child's share , and a later clause names "my said children or grandchildren" outright. George Augustus Kolbe died eleven months before his father. On paper his share therefore fell to his children at Burgersdorp — including Margaretha Kolbe, who married John Augustus Barry.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: What was searched → Why this archive exists In 1915 a man at Barkly East filled in his own mother's death notice. Where it asked for her parents' names, he wrote: "Father: Kolbe, thinks James was christian name . Mother: Unknown ." His grandfather was George Augustus Kolbe — who married at sixteen on a sworn lie in Shoreditch, sailed on the Nautilus in 1819 as an 1820 Settler , preached across the Orange River, and named a Karoo farm after the Württemberg his own father had left. His grandmother was Margaret Downing of London.

hits.title: The Barrys
hits.text: The 1820 Settler hypothesis does not survive arithmetic. He was born 8 June 1819 . The settler fleets sailed from late 1819 and reached Algoa Bay from April 1820. He cannot have been born on that voyage. But the family does have a documented 1820 Settler — his own father-in-law, George Augustus Kolbe , who sailed on the Nautilus from Gravesend on 3 December 1819. Inferred The likeliest reading is that a true settler story attached itself to the wrong branch.

hits.title: Open questions
hits.text: The single most important unopened door: it indexes Cape (KAB) and Transvaal (TAB) estate files and death notices , which is where a death notice for Willem Hermanus Booyzen would be found. Cape Archives (KAB), Master's Office (MOOC) — one reference is already in hand: MOOC 6/9/35: 7698 (1845) , the estate of George Augustus Kolbe. It has not been ordered or read. The Dutch Reformed Church registers for Graaff-Reinet, Cradock, Colesberg, Burgersdorp, Dordrecht and Barkly East — already the backbone of the tree's citations, but read only where FamilySearch has indexed them.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: Mother: Unknown ." His grandfather was George Augustus Kolbe — who married at sixteen on a sworn lie in Shoreditch, sailed on the Nautilus in 1819 as an 1820 Settler , preached across the Orange River, and named a Karoo farm after the Württemberg his own father had left. His grandmother was Margaret Downing of London. Both of them lie under a cut-stone monument at Burgersdorp — names, London birthplaces, farm and dates carved into it — about forty miles from where that notice was written. The family forgot them inside seventy years, with the headstone still standing. And it had happened before, on the other side of the house.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: AND THE ENTRY TWO LINES ABOVE IT IS THE OTHER THING. 2186, the same afternoon: AUGUSTUS KOLBE, father GEORGE FREDK ENSLIN, mother MARY ELIZABETH KOLBE. This site carried a contradiction marked Serious — Margaretha Kolbe appearing to marry Enslin while married to John Barry — and resolved it from Margaret Downing's 1867 death notice, which named a daughter Mary Elizabeth married to George F. Enslin. Here are the two sisters, baptising a son each, two entries apart, on one page. Six more baptisms from the same registers give exact birth dates to five Barry children, including the direct ancestor: CATHERINA MARY SOPHIA BARRY, BORN 4 AUGUST 1859, who has been “1859” on this site since it was built.

hits.title: Open questions
hits.text: § 12 · High priority Who is in the "Kolbe–Downing" photograph? A carte-de-visite captioned as George Augustus Kolbe and Margaret Downing cannot be them — the costume is c. 1875–1885, and they died in 1844 and 1867. The likeliest sitter is their son George Augustus Kolbe (b. 1836) . Where to look: the pencilled inscription on the card mount, at higher resolution than the tree holds; the photographer's imprint if the reverse survives; and the descendants who uploaded it. Also: who took it, and where.

hits.title: The Kolbes
hits.text: And one of them travels. Frederik Fortunatus Kolbe (1839) becomes Frederick Fortunatus Barry (1863) becomes Frederik Fortsenatus Booÿsen (1899) — one name carried across three surnames and sixty years, degrading slightly at each handover. The women → John Gottlob Kolbe, 1765–1845 — a tailor of Bond Street The tree leads with the German original, Johan Gottlieb . Four documents — his son's baptism register, his own will, his death certificate and his burial entry — all call him John Gottlob . That is the name he used in England, and the one this archive follows.

hits.title: The Kolbes
hits.text: They read exactly as a missionary's children's names should: scriptural, Latinate, chosen rather than inherited. And one of them travels. Frederik Fortunatus Kolbe (1839) becomes Frederick Fortunatus Barry (1863) becomes Frederik Fortsenatus Booÿsen (1899) — one name carried across three surnames and sixty years, degrading slightly at each handover. The women → John Gottlob Kolbe, 1765–1845 — a tailor of Bond Street The tree leads with the German original, Johan Gottlieb .

hits.title: The namesakes
hits.text: This archive keeps the two apart, and says which is which. One name, three surnames, no blood tie proved between two of them Fortunatus It comes out of the London Kolbes and ends up on a Booÿsen born in the year the war began. Who When What they are to the name Frederik Fortunatus Kolbe of the London Kolbes The source of the name. Frederick Fortunatus Barry — Carried into the Barrys by the Kolbe marriage of 1850. Frederik Fortsenatus Booÿsen b. 1899 And into the Booysens, spelled with a diaeresis, in 1899. Ruben, a Schoeman name, travels the same way into the Barrys — Ruben Jacobus Josuah Barry.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: The official record at the end of his life calls him simply an agriculturist , and he died on his own farm. Those are not contradictions — they are a life in sequence — but the archive should stop leading with "missionary". Ten children, and one who is missing The notice names ten. Keetor Peter Benjamin Kolbe , whom the tree gives a birth in 1840, is not among them — nor among the ten in his mother's 1867 notice. He died young, or he does not belong in this family. Julia Kolbe , whom MyHeritage flags as born two years after her father's death, is likewise absent, as she must be.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: The one death notice where line 3 works · Found TAB MHG 2945/44, read at full resolution off the film. Anna Johanna Maria Booyzen, born Pretorius, died Forest Hill 26 February 1944, aged 37. The parents line — blank or evasive on all four earlier notices in this archive — is filled in completely: Petrus Jacobus Pretorius and Margareth Wilhelmina Elizabeth Pretorius, both at 96 James Street, Germiston. The form did not change. The person filling it in did. Her husband signed it, and her parents were alive and reachable. Withdrawn — Maggie born 1 October 1926 · Taken back This archive carried Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth “Maggie” Booyzen’s birth as 1 October 1926, taken from the family tree.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: DOROTHEA REGINA AND RUBEN JACOBUS JOSUAH ARE NOT ON IT, and this archive had both as children “named on the 1915 death notice”. They are grandchildren: a Dorothea Regina baptised at Slang River in 1892 and a Ruben Jacobus Hosea at Dordrecht in 1888, both to Henry Nicholas Barry and Anna Johanna Maria Schoeman. The page also gives Margaretha Kolbe's death as 2 AUGUST 1912, where this archive had only the year. And it says the marriage took place at “Burghersdorp (probably)” — a son of the house, writing in English with a solicitor's help, who did not know where his parents married and put it in brackets.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: The tree is wrong three times over. Boomkweker Not a miner, and not yet a railwayman. In 1924 George grew trees. A wholly new occupation for him — and by 1947 he was a clerk on the South African Railways . Both were living at Evaton — where Anna's grandmother Anna Johanna Maria Schoeman had died the year before. The whole connection had moved north together. 1947 · The death registration, and a garbled memory vindicated Entry 10,899 , Johannesburg, registered 12 December 1947 — a second document, distinct from the death notice.

hits.text: The surname BARRY had never been searched. It returns four, and two are here: Fred J. Barry of Ivanhoe, Barkly East / Wodehouse, tried June 1901 — the same month as Daniel Willem Schoeman of Caerlaverock , in whose house the family married five weeks later — and Richard Peter Barry of Jerpoint , which is Kathleen Barry's brother's name. Identity unproven; the district is not. The rebels → The spelling was changed to avoid the "joiners" The change is on paper. The spelling was not new.

hits.text: 'Booyzen' returns nothing in any of the fifteen registers. THE SURNAME BARRY HAS NOW BEEN SEARCHED, as this entry said it should be, and it returns four: BARRY, FRED J., plaasboer of IVANHOE, district BARKLEY-OOS/WODEHOUSE, TRIED JUNE 1901 — the same district and the same month as Daniel Willem Schoeman of Caerlaverock, in whose house the family married five weeks later; BARRY, RICHARD PETER, plaasboer of JERPOINT — and Richard Peter Barry is Kathleen Barry's brother, the R. P. Barry who signed his mother's 1915 death notice at Manorowen, Barkly East; plus Adolf Barry of Keimoes and Thomas Andrew Barry of Oudtshoorn, neither relevant.

tersia-booyzen.r: Recorded the name-change and Anglo-Boer War account on the MyHeritage tree, as told to her by her father. It is FAMILY TESTIMONY AND NOT FROM A DOCUMENT — which is exactly why this archive quotes it in full and then tests it against the Cape Rebel rolls and the surname distribution, rather than repeating it.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: The documents → Ways in Search everything Everyone 78 The places 28 Our line, drawn The timeline 43 The atlas The plates 83 What was searched 30 What the family remembers, and how it has held up One long piece of testimony sits at the centre of this archive — recorded on the family tree from Tersia Booyzen , told to her by her father. It carries seven separate claims. None of them has yet been proved. Two are already in trouble, and three now have strong circumstantial support that did not exist before this archive was built.

hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: Documented He was not shot by anybody. The death registration → Inferred Three readings survive, and the archive does not choose between them: The generations are miscounted. Tersia Booyzen was counting from herself, not from the current researcher. Her "great great grandfather" may be a man this archive has not identified. "Shot and killed" is not an execution. It may mean killed in action, or shot during a farm clearance — neither of which would appear on the treason lists.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: This archive has not seen the medal, the ABO application, or Schroeder's signature. It is strong secondary evidence, and the prisoner number is what ties it to the register rather than to a name alone. The family's own war testimony now has something to be tested against. This archive has quoted Tersia Booyzen's account in full for the whole project and measured it only against surname distributions and rebel district figures, because there was no record. There is one now: a policeman of Pretoria who was at Talana in the first week of the war, wounded at Wagon Hill, present at Spion Kop and at the ZARPs' last stand, taken at Tolosberg with forty-one others and two guns, and shipped to India.

hits.title: The name
hits.text: The claim being tested "There were some Booysens who were joiners, fighting on the side of the British, so our great grandfather changed the spelling to Booyzen so as not to be associated with them." — family testimony recorded on the MyHeritage tree from Tersia Booyzen. The full account → Documented That a change happened is on the record twice over. MyHeritage carries "Former name: Booysen" as a formal Name Change fact on Willem Hermanus "William Henry" Booyzen (1851–1905) — and, far better, both spellings appear on a single sheet of paper in September 1905 .
